calculator.title: Salary calculator
calculator.intro: How much you take home after taxes and contributions
calculator.enterAmount: Enter an amount to see the breakdown.
calculator.assumptions: Calculated for a single person without children on an employment contract, 2026 rules.

notes.EE: Estonia: tax-free allowance of €700 a month, 2% to the second pension pillar.
notes.LV: Latvia: tax-free allowance of €550 a month, 10.5% social insurance on income up to €105,300 a year.
notes.LT: Lithuania: tax-free allowance of up to €747 a month that shrinks as pay grows; 19.5% contributions (without the second pension pillar, whose members pay 3% more).
notes.PL: Poland: taxes are calculated in złoty at the ECB rate of {{date}} (€1 = {{rate}} zł); standard employee costs of 250 zł a month; without PPK and without the under-26 relief.
notes.DE: Germany: tax class I, no church tax, no children (+0.6% care insurance), public health insurance with the average 2.9% add-on; income tax includes the solidarity surcharge where it applies.
notes.BG: Bulgaria: 13.78% contributions on income up to €2,300 a month (€2,111.64 before August), 10% income tax with no tax-free allowance.
notes.RO: Romania: taxes are calculated in lei at the ECB rate of {{date}} (€1 = {{rate}} lei); 25% pension, 10% health, 10% income tax; the personal deduction for pay up to 6,325 lei a month is approximate.
notes.HU: Hungary: taxes are calculated in forints at the ECB rate of {{date}} (€1 = {{rate}} Ft); 18.5% contribution and 15% income tax on the whole salary; without the under-25 and mothers’ exemptions.
notes.CZ: Czechia: taxes are calculated in koruna at the ECB rate of {{date}} (€1 = {{rate}} Kč); 11.6% contributions do not reduce the tax; 15% income tax (23% above 1,762,812 Kč a year) minus a 2,570 Kč monthly credit.
notes.SK: Slovakia: 14.4% contributions (5% health from 2026); the €5,966.73 yearly tax-free part shrinks for higher pay; 19–35% income tax; no children.
notes.AT: Austria: 18.07% social insurance (17.07% on the 13th and 14th salaries); the 13th and 14th are taxed at 6% after a €620 exemption; salaried employee without children or commuter allowance.
notes.IE: Ireland: 20% tax up to €44,000 and 40% above minus €4,000 of credits; USC 0.5–8%; PRSI 4.2% (4.35% from October 2026).
notes.CY: Cyprus: no tax up to €22,000 a year (2026 reform); 8.8% social insurance and 2.65% GESY; without the 50% expat exemption.
notes.MT: Malta: single rates 0–35%; 10% social security, at most €55.93 a week; without statutory bonuses and COLA.
notes.GR: Greece: 13.37% EFKA; 9–44% income tax minus a credit of up to €777; no children, over 25.
notes.HR: Croatia: 20% pension contribution, €600 monthly personal allowance, Zagreb rates of 23% and 33% (above €5,000 of monthly base); health insurance is paid by the employer.
notes.SI: Slovenia: 23.1% contributions (incl. 1% long-term care) plus a fixed €39.36 monthly health contribution; €5,551.93 general allowance; 16–50% tax; without the extra allowance for low pay.
notes.NL: Netherlands: employees pay no separate social contributions — they are built into the 35.75–49.5% tax rates; minus the general and labour tax credits; no employer pension fund, no 30% expat ruling.
notes.BE: Belgium: 13.07% social security plus the special social security contribution; 30% employee expenses (up to €5,930); 25–50% tax with a reduction for the €11,550 tax-free amount; 7% municipal surcharge.
notes.LU: Luxembourg: tax class 1; 3.05% health, 8.5% pension, 1.4% care insurance; 0–42% tax (2025 scale) plus 7% employment fund surcharge; without the employee tax credit (CIS).
notes.FR: France: non-executive private-sector employee, 1 tax share; ~21% contributions (pension, AGIRC-ARRCO, CSG/CRDS) without mutuelle; 0–45% tax after the 10% deduction and the décote.
notes.IT: Italy: 9.19% INPS; 23/33/43% IRPEF minus the employee and tax-wedge credits; regional and municipal surcharges ~2.5% (vary by city); income up to €20,000 gets a tax-free bonus, so tax can be negative.
notes.ES: Spain: 6.5% social security up to €5,101.20 a month; 19–47% IRPF on the general scale (regional part varies), €5,550 personal allowance, €2,000 other expenses.
notes.PT: Portugal: 11% social security; 12.2–48% IRS (reduced 2026 rates), €4,587.09 specific deduction; without IRS Jovem or expense deductions.
notes.FI: Finland: 7.3% pension, 0.89% unemployment, 0.88% sickness; 12.64–37.5% state tax and 7.57% municipal (average), 1.10% health care contribution and Yle tax included in the tax line; no church tax.
notes.SE: Sweden: taxes are calculated in kronor at the ECB rate of {{date}} (€1 = {{rate}} kr); 32.38% municipal tax (average), 20% state tax above 643,000 kr; the 7% pension fee is refunded as a tax reduction; without burial and church fees.
notes.DK: Denmark: taxes are calculated in kroner at the ECB rate of {{date}} (€1 = {{rate}} kr); 8% AM-bidrag and ATP; 25% municipal tax (average) and 12.01% state tax (+7.5% above 641,200 kr); no church tax.

calculator.paymentsNote: Salary here is paid {{count}} times a year, so “per month” means one payment.
